title: Orchestrated benchmark profiles and traffic-simulation harness for kernel/attention scheduling
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Deliver a reproducible, configurable harness that synthesizes realistic inference traffic and produces canonical performance profiles for kernel routing, attention optimizations, and prefill/decode scheduling. The harness will: 1) emit mixed workloads (short prompts, long prefill-heavy sequences, high-traffic small queries, and few-shot decode-heavy flows); 2) exercise kernel selection heuristics and attention-optimization toggles; 3) produce golden-baseline artifacts (p95/p99 latency, token throughput, memory, and KV-cache hit stats) that can be used as CI perf gates.

Scope and acceptance criteria:
- Harness can replay traffic traces and generate synthetic mixes by weighting trace buckets (latency distribution + seq length + temperature/beam settings).
- Supports toggles: kernel routing policies, attention algorithm variants (local-window, block-sparse, causal-approx), and prefill vs. decode batching knobs.
- Generates artifacts: per-model CSV time-series, aggregated golden baseline JSON, and dashboard-ready throughput/latency graphs.
- Integrates into CI: a workflow that compares a pull-request run to golden baseline and produces pass/fail with thresholds and statistical confidence.
- Documentation: runbook describing how to add new workload profiles and interpret CI failures.

Implementation plan:
1) Build a traffic-simulator CLI service that converts traces and random generators into a stream of requests with configurable mix weights and target RPS.
2) Extend the microbench harness to allow toggling kernel-routing flags and attention opt flags at runtime and capture low-level telemetry (kernel selection count, op timings, KV-cache hit/miss).
3) Define a canonical baseline generator: run N warmup runs, then M measured runs (configurable) and compute bootstrapped p95/p99 with variance. Artifacts stored in S3 and a stable baseline repo.
4) Add CI integration: a GitHub Actions job that spins up a minimal harness VM (or reuses a long-lived perf runner), runs the benchmark subset, and reports regressions to the PR with link to artifact diff.
5) Dashboard and alerting: publish to perf dashboard (Grafana) and wire perf regression alerts to #perf-regressions on Slack.

Decision trade-offs noted:
- We will not try to run full-production-scale traffic in CI; CI will use representative subsets and rely on canary runs for full-scale validation.
- To keep CI latency low we will use bootstrapped statistical testing over smaller sample sizes; threshold tuning will be conservative to avoid false positives.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-perf-harness-design
- Prototype PR for traffic-sim: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1429
- Baseline storage: s3://redwood-perf/baselines/runtime-1.20/
